🇮🇱 🇺🇸 ‘Nothing has been finalized’: Israel’s defense establishment unafraid of US aid cuts Israeli defense officials slapped down the Finance Ministry’s alarmist sentiments about a potential requirement to continue buying tens of billions of dollars’ worth of American weaponry even if US security assistance was canceled. The Senate Appropriations Committee’s 2027 draft budget includes “all the funding for Israeli aid under the memorandum of understanding (MOU). It could come up for a vote and be removed, but as far as 2027 is concerned, we are certainly not saying this money is unavailable,” a defense source told JPost. The potential $31B shortfall outlined by the Finance Ministry is inaccurate, the source added, noting that Israel’s actual commitments after 2028 amount to $16B, and that the government has approved a “shekel-denominated budget allocation” for purchases should US aid become unavailable. Earlier this month, President Trump surprised Israeli officials by pledging to end US military aid to Israel at the end of 2026. But appropriations are the prerogative of Congress, and the current 10-year military assistance pledge will remain in place through 2028. While some of the new lawmakers elected in the Democrats’ midterms sweep have pledged to cut aid, hundreds were also congratulated for their victories by AIPAC . The $3.8B in annual aid inside the ten-year MOU is only a small part of the aid Israel gets from Washington. It’s also received nearly $18B in supplemental military funding in the last three years, and tens of billions in direct and indirect economic and fiscal assistance, investments, and other support . 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime
